minutes.headline: Finance Committee reviewed the FY21 budget gap, debt and capital plan, and discussed levying to the limit; no budget vote
minutes.summary: The committee continued its FY21 budget review during the COVID-19 period. It discussed whether to levy to the limit, how levy limit and excess capacity rules work, and what help exists for stressed taxpayers. It then reviewed the debt schedule and revised capital plan, heard public comment on state aid, encumbrances and public works projects, set upcoming meetings, and adjourned by roll call.

public_comment.topic: Asked about the ten percent state aid reduction, encumbering funds as an alternative to cuts, the thin margin of the gap, and the lag in meals tax receipts.
Said the fuel tank plan puts the tanks inside conservation and riverfront jurisdiction, risking delay and added cost.

votes.motion: Motion to adjourn, taken by roll call.

budget_items.what_was_said: A member raised the gap and asked what tax relief it could translate to if not spent.
Debt for the primary school and public safety complex drops off, partly offset by the end of MSBA reimbursement.
A final MSBA payment is expected after the board met, with a final local portion to bond.
The last bond for the middle/high school and pavement management is small, with minimal tax impact.
The town received state money for the fuel tanks; capital article funds carry over until closeout.
A speaker estimated delay and added cost from the tank location.
A speaker said the gap equals roughly a ten percent state aid cut and about two percent of the budget.

decisions.decision: Discussed starting the following week's public hearing meeting earlier, at 6:30; the chair noted recommendations on the warrant will be made on the 7th and the report is due the 14th.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee took no votes and continued its FY21 budget review, including a discussion of whether to levy to the limit.
Members discussed the budget gap, when reserves might be tapped, and what tax relief the gap could represent if not spent.
The committee reviewed the debt schedule: primary school and public safety complex debt drops off, partly offset by the end of state school-building reimbursement.
A speaker in public comment said the fuel tank plan places the tanks within conservation and riverfront jurisdiction, risking delay and added cost.
The chair discussed starting the next public hearing meeting earlier, at 6:30; warrant recommendations are due on the 7th and the report on the 14th.

why_it_matters: Whether the town levies to its limit, and how much of the budget gap is closed by cuts, reserves or taxes, decides what residents pay on the next tax bill.
Debt that is ending lowers what residents pay for past building projects, so it affects how much room the town has under the levy limit.
